_what: Spire attack (pso-roguelike new-features/roguelike/design/mechanics/aanval.md par. 2 and 7): the data of the reward weapons beyond the reward grid (system/spire-rewards.json). No code reads this file yet: SpireAttack.cc and SpireRewardWeapon.cc will, at every reward draw. Enabled false is the data-only switch: the reward weapons are the grid's cells again, with the grid's own grind, special and Hit, no restart needed. Attribute: a reward weapon drawn in room k (1 = the first room of the episode) carries the attribute against the enemies of room k + 1 (the last room: its own). AreaOfRoom is Sega's area column 0-9 of a room (Forest 1 ... Ruins 3; a boss by Sega's own link, ItemCreator::table_index_for_area: Dragon Cave 1, De Rol Le Mine 1, Vol Opt Ruins 1, Dark Falz Ruins 3), AreaAttribute the attribute Sega's BonusTypeProbTable gives most in that column, AttributeIds its type in data1[6], [8] and [10]. Its value in percent is AttrPct of the tier + AttrPerRung per difficulty rung (0 Normal - 3 Ultimate) + AttrPerStepAboveW6 per weapon level the rung lifts the room above W6 (RoomW + RungWeaponSteps of the grid), at most AttrCap. SecondAttr: from that rung on, that tier also carries the attribute of the first later room whose attribute is another one, at Percent of the first value (no such room: no second attribute). Hit is the grid's plus HitPerRung per rung, at most HitCap. Rares: per rung, class, line and tier (Epic, Legendary) Sega's rare weapons, strongest first (ATPMin + ATPMax of Sega's item table, then stars, then code). The server gives the first one the run copy can carry with rule B's mag, the mag's level (5 plus the POW, DEX and MIND the weapon asks, as the grid counts it) at most MagCap of the room's weapon level (the grid's WeaponLevels key MagCapKey names, copied here because the server does not read it there); when none fits, the grid's cell. RareFloor true: a rare weapon comes with the grind it needs, at most its MaxGrind, to be no weaker than the Normal weapon of the same cell with its grind (strength: ATPMin + ATPMax + 4 per grind); a Legendary one is held against what Epic gives in the same room as well, and Legendary gives Epic's weapon when its own cannot reach it. RareFloor false: no grind on a rare weapon. A weapon is listed when it is a rare weapon (9 stars or more) of the line (KindLines: Sega's WeaponKind to the grid's line), the class can equip it (Sega's UsabilityFlags), Sega's Episode 1 rare table drops it on a difficulty Columns names for the rung and tier, and the copy can carry it in at least one room of the rung. Legendary holds every Epic weapon as well, so Legendary is never weaker than Epic. Items names every listed weapon and its line (the line a reward follows when the player holds it). RareSpecials: Sega's weapon specials a drawn weapon can get, by play style and by Sega's stars, [id, name]: Element (Ice, Bind, Heat and Shock families), Recover (Draw and Heart), Gamble (Charge, Spirit, Berserk, Devil's, Demon's) and Trick (Dim and Panic). ExcludedSpecials: All is never drawn (the experience specials; a rare weapon's built-in special stays), Android never for HUcast, HUcaseal, RAcast and RAcaseal (they have no TP: the specials that steal or cost it). Items and Rares are DERIVED: sh tests/spire-attack-table.test.sh --write rewrites them from Sega's tables and the grid; the same script without --write is the test of every row. Edit the other keys by hand, then run it with --write.
